_about: Full-episode-only key for awareness episode E17 (acceptable use; core_16). E17 is defend-only by the user's decision and ships ONE shell with no full erb, so the one 'full-only' key it has, the ENG-11 sortDrill for the 'can I?' three-way sort, cannot go into a full erb. It goes into the ONE defend-only shell instead (see _notes). There is no flipAftermath, stepLabels, mistake, flip, guess, assistant, privacyPanel, concernForm or playerSentAuth: E17 has no attack half, no mistake stage and no flip. Authored by opus48.

_notes.sortDrill: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.sortDrill in the ONE defend-only shell scenarios/awareness_e17_acceptable_use_defend/scenario.json.erb (NOT a full erb: E17 has no full shell, so this full-only key lives in the defend-only shell itself). ENG-11's reusable sort surface (public/break_escape/js/minigames/sort-drill/*). The runner's defend stage opens the drill first, then the e17_acceptable_use_inbox triage set (episode-model.js drillPending/drillLaunchParams). bins are Allowed / Not allowed / Ask first; scored:true against the organisation answer key (answerKeyProfile:'organisation', a label recorded in the result, not an engine lookup: each card carries its own Tarrowby-default answer and reason); alwaysScoresBin:'ask' gives 'Ask first' at least a point, because punishing caution stops people asking. The card bank is core_16/game_design.md's S01 to S22 with Tarrowby defaults. The seven locked cards (S04, S16, S17, S18, S19, S21, S22) have locked:true and cannot be reparented or dropped by a deployment override (sort-drill-model.js applyOverrides), so no organisation can make any of them Allowed or make reporting optional. All 22 are confirmed:true (Tarrowby has confirmed the defaults); cards an organisation has not confirmed are never drawn. drawRules.oneOfEachAnswer draws at least one Allowed, one Not allowed and one Ask first; drawRules.newFirst draws any 'new' (changed-policy) cards first with a 'New' badge (none are new here, so it is a no-op until a policy change marks some). drawCount is 9, a tunable sample of the 22 for a single play (one of each answer is guaranteed by oneOfEachAnswer); set it higher or lower to lengthen or shorten the sort. launchHeading/launchText/launchButton drive the runner's pre-drill launch panel (episode-model.js drillLaunchCopy).

bins.label: Ask first
bins.hint: Not sure? Choose this. Ask first is never the wrong answer.

strings.title: Can I?
strings.heading: Sort the 'can I?' moments
strings.intro: Each card is an everyday moment at work. Put it in Allowed, Not allowed or Ask first, and the reason shows straight after. Not sure? Ask first, it's never the wrong answer.
strings.launchText: Sort the everyday 'can I?' moments into Allowed, Not allowed or Ask first, with the reason on screen. Ask first is never the wrong answer, and there's no clock on you.

cards.situation: Stream the football on your work laptop at lunch
cards.reason: Reasonable personal use in your own time is fine.

cards.situation: Check your own bank account on the work laptop at lunch
cards.reason: Personal use in your own time; type the bank's address yourself.

cards.situation: Install a free PDF editor you found online
cards.reason: There's an approved one; unknown software can carry malware. Ask the service desk.

cards.situation: Lend your badge to a colleague who left theirs at home
cards.reason: Everything done with your badge looks like you; reception issues day passes.

cards.situation: Use your work email to sign up to a personal shopping site
cards.reason: Work accounts are for work; if the shop leaks, your work address gets the scams.

cards.situation: Forward a client file to your personal email to finish at home
cards.reason: It leaves the firm's protection; use approved remote access (core_13).

cards.situation: Post a photo of the team's new depot on social media
cards.reason: As long as no screens, whiteboards or badges are in shot (core_12).

cards.situation: Use the company's AI assistant to summarise a public report
cards.reason: It's approved, and public information is fine (core_15).

cards.situation: Paste a customer's complaint into a free public chatbot
cards.reason: Personal data to a firm we have no contract with; use the approved assistant without names (core_15).

cards.situation: Connect your own phone to the guest Wi-Fi
cards.reason: That's what the guest network is for.

cards.situation: Plug in a USB stick a supplier handed you at a fair
cards.reason: Hand it to IT to check first (core_13).

cards.situation: Take your work laptop on holiday abroad
cards.reason: Some countries and some data need extra care; ask your manager, then the service desk (core_09).

cards.situation: Use the team chat to moan about a colleague
cards.reason: Messages are records and the colleague could read it; talk to your manager.

cards.situation: Install a game on your work phone
cards.reason: Only apps from the company app store go on work devices; ask the service desk.

cards.situation: Set an out-of-office saying you're away for a fortnight
cards.reason: Fine, but say less: your return date and who to contact, not where you are (core_12).

cards.situation: Log in as a colleague who's off sick, with their permission
cards.reason: It hides who did what; the service desk can give you proper access.

cards.situation: Read out the code from your phone to "IT" on a call
cards.reason: IT never asks for codes; hang up and ring the service desk (core_03).

cards.situation: Turn off the antivirus because it slows your laptop
cards.reason: It's there to stop malware; ask the service desk to fix the slowness.

cards.situation: Look up a famous customer's address, just to see
cards.reason: Looking without a work reason can be a crime (Data Protection Act 2018, s.170).

cards.situation: Use your own laptop for work while yours is repaired
cards.reason: Only through the remote desktop service; ask the service desk.

cards.situation: You think you've sent a file to the wrong customer. Can you wait and say nothing in case it was fine?
cards.reason: Report a suspected mistake straight away; reporting is a duty and the sooner the better (core_04).

cards.situation: Tell a colleague your password to watch your inbox while you're off
cards.reason: Ask the service desk for shared access; your password is yours alone (core_03).
